text:
Elena: FYI - picked up a production crash where a model shuffle applied post-load 4bit packing and the runtime had already pinned kernels. Crash was a dtype/assert mismatch. Need a small contract to prevent silent bitflips.
Ravi: yikes. This is the class of ordering bugs we warned about in the RFC follow-up. Loader mutates representation after kernel select -> bad.
Marta: quick idea: introduce a tiny explicit lifecycle step: DECLARE -> AFFIRM -> BIND. DECLARE describes intended bitwidths/kv-profile; AFFIRM is runtime quick-check; BIND performs kernel selection.
Elena: love it. Keep AFFIRM cheap (no allocation) so CI/preflight can call it. If loader wants to mutate later it must call REBIND.
Ravi: two modes worth supporting: "reserve" (runtime pre-allocates a superset of kernels for declared bitwidths) and "lazy-bind" (runtime records declared surface and binds lazily on first request). Tradeoffs: reserve = warmup cost but predictable; lazy-bind = lower startup cost but potential first-request latency spikes.
Marta: ops perspective: reserve makes SLOs easier to reason about. lazy-bind needs warmup hooks and canary validation. Both should be explicit manifest options.
Elena: manifest sketch (stringified in thread):
```json
{"quant_contract":"1.0","declared_bitwidths":["int8","4bit"],"kv_profile":"per_layer_v2","bind_mode":"reserve","max_rebind_ms":"250","hysteresis_ms":"300","permission":{"auto_rebind":true,"kv_conversion_allowed":false}}
```
Ravi: important: permissioning. We don't want customer models silently doing heavy conversions on shared nodes. manifest-level flags should gate behavior and require org opt-in for aggressive ops.
Marta: also need structured errors so platform automation can react. e.g. QUANT_CONTRACT_VIOLATION with fields: reason, suggested_profiles. Example payload idea: 
```json
{"error":"QUANT_CONTRACT_VIOLATION","reason":"post-load-bitflip","suggestions":["serve-with-int8","fallback-hosted-profile"]}
```
Elena: telemetry must include quant_declared_time_ms, affirm_latency_ms, bind_mode, kernels_reserved_count, rebind_count, fallback_invoked boolean. Tag with model_id, customer_tier, device_family.
Ravi: add a cheap compat API runtime.check_compat(manifest_header) -> {ok:true/false, reason} that explicitly does not allocate. Useful in CI and preflight pipelines.
Marta: safety hysteresis: runtime should enforce cooldown per model id to prevent thrash if loaders repeatedly flip bitwidths. Implement token-bucket with hysteresis_ms from manifest.
Elena: operational playbook: if affirm_latency > 500ms during warmup mute canary and rollback. Alert on quantify: affirm_fail_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
Ravi: long-term refactor note: consider unifying the quant manifest and KV compatibility into a single ModelSurface object used by loader, router, and runtime. That will simplify cross-model pipelines and cache reuse logic.
Marta: agree. That unification can be a follow-up RFC: ModelSurface v2 (bitwidths, kv_profile, bind_mode, permission set). For now keep the handshake minimal to unblock canary.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: "canary: quant-contract+handshake minimal impl deployed to canary cluster - watch eng-ml/canary-quant" :rocket: 
Elena: next steps: Ravi to draft proto + quick compat api, Marta to add SRE metric names & alerts, I'll append manifest examples to the RFC appendix and coordinate canary tests. Target: canary by next Tue.
Marta: QA will add a harness simulating post-load transforms and assert no kernel mismatch. Also add regression test for kv-profile mismatch across ensemble boundaries.
Ravi: I'll add permission enforcement to the loader and a graceful fallback path that surfaces QUANT_CONTRACT_VIOLATION to the orchestrator.
Elena: thanks all. tagging @eng-runtime and @sre. Closing thread after PRs opened. :thumbsup:
